title: The plague
hookLine: Umar turns back from a plague region, and a companion quotes the Prophet ﷺ: don't enter or leave a plague land (Bukhari)

lines: A CARAVAN HALTED ON THE ROAD.
cards: A caravan is halted on the road north. At its head is Umar, on his way to Syria.

Riding out to meet him come his commanders, Abu Ubaydah among them, and they bring news nobody wants: plague has broken out in the land ahead. Behind Umar ride companions of the Prophet, emigrants and Ansar.
Ahead is a sickness no one can see. Do you go on, trusting God? Or do you turn around?

teach.b: Bukhari tells it in detail. Umar calls the early emigrants and asks them. They disagree: some say go on, some say turn back.
He calls the Ansar of Medina. They disagree too. Then he calls the elders of Quraysh, and they speak with one voice: turn back, don't lead the people into the plague.
So Umar announces they will leave in the morning. And Abu Ubaydah, his old friend, objects: are you running from the decree of God? Umar answers with a picture.

teach.h: FROM GOD'S DECREE TO GOD'S DECREE.
teach.b: Yes, we are running from the decree of God to the decree of God.

teach.h: TWO SLOPES, ONE GREEN, ONE BARE.
teach.b: If you had camels and came to a valley with two slopes, one green and one bare, and you grazed them on the green, wouldn't that be by God's decree? And if you grazed them on the bare, wouldn't that be by God's decree too?
Choosing the safer slope is not leaving God's will. It is moving within it.

teach.h: ABD AL-RAHMAN: I HEARD THE PROPHET.
teach.b: Then a companion who had been away arrives: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. I have knowledge of this, he says.
I heard the Messenger of God say: if you hear of it in a land, don't go into it; and if it breaks out in a land where you are, don't leave it to flee from it. Umar praises God, and turns back.
Notice the order: Umar consulted, decided, and then found that the Prophet's teaching agreed. Many readers today hear in those two lines what's now called quarantine.

how: Muslim scholars cite the Prophet's teaching on plague, and Umar's turning back, when giving guidance on epidemics: avoid entering an affected place, and don't flee from one.

o: a war that broke out on the road to Syria
a drought that dried the wells of Medina
the outbreak that turned Umar back from Syria

p: are you running from God's decree?
from God's decree to God's decree
I heard the Messenger of God

s: Umar turned back only after hearing the hadith
he had already decided after consulting; Abd al-Rahman's report confirmed it.
the Prophet's teaching forbids fleeing a plague land
if it breaks out where you are, don't leave it to flee from it.
the early emigrants all agreed with each other
they disagreed, and so did the Ansar. the elders of Quraysh spoke with one voice.

games.q: you're Umar, on the road to Syria with the Prophet's companions. plague has broken out ahead, and your advisers disagree. what do you do?
o: go on alone and send the others home.
games.why: he turned back, saying: we run from God's decree to God's decree. then Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf recalled the Prophet: don't enter a plague land, don't flee one.

practice: Bring to mind one piece of good health advice you've been putting off: seeing a doctor, staying home when you're sick, taking a medicine properly, resting. Hear Umar: we run from God's decree to God's decree.
In his picture, taking care is not a lack of trust; the green slope is still God's slope.

wordCard.voice: The plague. The outbreak that turned Umar back on the road to Syria, and the Prophet's teaching, recalled by Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: don't go into a plague land, and don't flee from one. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: plague, the word in the Prophet's teaching about entering and leaving.

carryVoice: Your line: don't enter, don't leave. And the week: riddah, a will, a calendar, a register, Jerusalem, a Coptic boy, and a caravan turned back. That's the week.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5729 (Umar at Sargh; consultation; 'from God's decree to God's decree'; Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's hadith)
